apparatus_caveat: Only the selected collect entries have been transcribed and independently checked, not the entire formularies or books. Each is one continuous priestly block. Printed shortened conclusions Per. and Per Dominum nostrum. are retained without supplying a doxology. Abbreviations, long s, u/v, ae ligatures and line layout are normalized as declared in the artifacts. The separate retained pages establish the changed Gospel and Sunday heading; those observations are not represented as full Gospel transcriptions. Printing dates do not date the introduction of the changes; intervening editions and immediate ancestry remain unestablished.
basis: The complete printed collect entries in two Suscepimus Deus formularies perform the same liturgical function but are different compositions: Deus cuius providentia in 1550 and Largire nobis in 1604. The named formulary supplies the pairing anchor. The earlier heading is Dominica octava after Trinity; the later heading is Dominica sexta after the octave of Trinity. No identical numbered Sunday is assumed.
